issues.legal_issue: Taxes imposed under laws governing a union territory constitute Union taxation for purposes of the constitutional immunity of state property.
material_facts: Municipal laws in force in the territory imposed property taxes on land and buildings, including property owned by state governments.
The municipal law governing one area had been extended to the territory by parliamentary legislation, and the municipal laws governing the other areas were enacted by Parliament.
The dispute concerned property taxes imposed on state-owned property situated within a union territory.
issues.conclusion: The property taxes imposed under the municipal laws constitute Union taxation.
issues.legal_principle: Article 289(1) exempts state property from Union taxation. Under Article 246(4), Parliament has power to legislate for territories outside the States, including on matters in the State List. The Court relied on the majority ruling in In Re the Sea Customs Act that state property in a union territory is exempt from Union taxation on property, reaffirmed in Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation v. Income Tax Officer. It also relied on T.M. Kanniyan v. Income Tax Officer for Parliament’s plenary legislative power over union territories, and Mithan Lal v. State of Delhi for the principle that a law extended to a territory by Parliament derives force there from the parliamentary enactment.

predicates.property_tax_dispute_proceeding: A proceeding concerns a tax imposed on property.
predicates.state_owned_property_in_union_territory: A state government owns property situated in a territory that is not part of a State.
predicates.taxing_law_has_parliamentary_force: The law imposing the tax was enacted by Parliament or was extended to the territory by parliamentary legislation.

issues.definition: When a property-tax proceeding concerns state-owned property in a union territory and the taxing law has parliamentary force, the tax is Union taxation.

issues.legal_issue: State property in a union territory is exempt from property taxation when it is not used or occupied for a state trade or business.
material_facts: Municipal enactments imposed property taxes on property within their jurisdictions and expressly exempted Union property, but did not expressly exempt state property.
State governments owned property in the territory, and the tax claims against that property were based on the constitutional exemption for state property.
The case required the Court to determine the effect of the constitutional exemption together with the exception for trade or business.
issues.conclusion: Property owned by a state government is exempt from the property tax unless it is used or occupied for the purposes of a trade or business carried on by or on behalf of that government.
issues.legal_principle: Article 289(1) exempts the property and income of a State from Union taxation, subject to Article 289(2); Article 289(3) permits Parliament to declare a trade or business incidental to ordinary governmental functions and thereby outside the exception in clause (2). The Court relied on Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation v. Income Tax Officer for reading the clauses as an integrated scheme in which clause (2) qualifies clause (1) and clause (3) qualifies clause (2).

rule.if: state_property_tax_dispute_proceeding and state_government_owns_property and property_is_in_union_territory and not property_used_for_state_trade_or_business

predicates.state_property_tax_dispute_proceeding: A proceeding concerns property taxation claimed against property owned by a state government.
predicates.state_government_owns_property: A state government owns the property subject to the tax claim.
predicates.property_is_in_union_territory: The property is situated in a territory that is not part of a State.
predicates.property_used_for_state_trade_or_busines: The state government uses or occupies the property for a trade or business carried on by or on its behalf.

issues.definition: In a state-property tax proceeding concerning property in a union territory, property not used for the state government’s trade or business is not subject to the tax.

issues.legal_issue: Property owned by a state government is taxable when it is used or occupied for the purposes of a profit-motivated trade or business carried on by or on behalf of that government.
material_facts: The municipal enactments imposed property taxes on property within their jurisdictions and did not expressly exempt state property.
The Court construed the exception for state trade or business as requiring a profit motive, and distinguished such activity from governmental activity that merely results in some profit.

The municipal laws applied property taxes to property used or occupied for the purposes of such trade or business, even though they did not expressly state that they were enacted under the constitutional provision permitting such taxation.
issues.conclusion: Property used or occupied for the purposes of a profit-motivated state trade or business is subject to the property tax under the municipal enactments.
issues.legal_principle: Article 289(2) permits taxation, to the extent provided by parliamentary law, of state trade or business, connected operations, property used or occupied for those purposes, and related income; Article 289(3) allows Parliament to exclude specified trades or businesses incidental to ordinary governmental functions. The Court relied on Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation v. Income Tax Officer for the relationship between clauses (1), (2), and (3); on the presumption of constitutionality described in Charanjit Lal Chowdhary v. Union of India, Burrakur Coal Co. v. Union of India, Rt. Rev. Msgr. Mark Netto v. State of Kerala, Sanjeev Coke Manufacturing Co. v. Bharat Coking Coal, and Ram Krishna Dalmia v. Justice Tendolkar; and on In Re the Delhi Laws Act concerning limits on delegated policy-making. It held that the municipal enactments could be sustained under Article 289(2) to the extent they taxed property used for the relevant trade or business, without requiring express citation of that Article in the enactments.

rule.if: state_property_tax_dispute_proceeding and state_government_owns_property and municipal_tax_applies_to_property and property_used_for_profit_motivated_state_trade_or_business

predicates.state_property_tax_dispute_proceeding: A proceeding concerns property taxation claimed against property owned by a state government.
predicates.state_government_owns_property: A state government owns the property subject to the tax claim.
predicates.municipal_tax_applies_to_property: A municipal taxing law applies a property tax to the property.
predicates.property_used_for_profit_motivated_state: The state government uses or occupies the property for a trade or business carried on with a profit motive by or on its behalf.

issues.definition: When a state government’s property is subject to a municipal tax and is used for its profit-motivated trade or business, the property tax may be imposed on that property.

issues.legal_issue: A ruling that makes some state property taxable after a prior judgment treated all such property as exempt operates prospectively when prior assessments were not made in reliance on that judgment.
material_facts: The judgment under appeal had treated state properties as exempt in full.
No assessments had been made while that judgment governed the dispute.
The ruling that replaced the full exemption could make some state properties liable to tax.
issues.legal_principle: The Court invoked Article 142 of the Constitution to limit the temporal operation of its judgment, having regard to the prior judgment, the absence of assessments, and the circumstances of the inter-governmental dispute.

predicates.state_property_tax_dispute_proceeding: A proceeding concerns property taxation claimed against property owned by a state government.
predicates.prior_ruling_exempted_all_state_property: An earlier ruling treated all state-owned property in the relevant territory as exempt from the tax.
predicates.no_assessments_were_made_under_prior_rul: Tax assessments were not made while the earlier ruling governed the dispute.
predicates.new_ruling_makes_some_state_property_tax: The new ruling makes at least some state-owned property liable to the tax.

issues.definition: When an earlier ruling exempted all state property, no assessments were made under it, and the new ruling makes some such property taxable, the new ruling operates prospectively.
